basis: Cerebral arterial stenosis defines moyamoya; infarction or hemorrhagic brain injury occurs in over ~30% during the usual symptomatic course.

decisions.neurologic: involved: permanent ischemic or hemorrhagic brain injury affects over ~30% during the symptomatic course; transient ischemic attacks alone would not qualify.

basis: Thymic epithelial carcinoma has no covered anatomical axis; neuroendocrine differentiation alone establishes neither endocrine gland disease nor immune disease.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: neuroendocrine histology in a thymic carcinoma does not establish origin in an endocrine gland or a metabolic disorder.

basis: Lower motor neuron degeneration defines the disease; weakness and denervation atrophy reflect neural injury rather than direct muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting is secondary to denervation; the disease directly damages motor neurons rather than skeletal muscle.

basis: Synostosis, eyelid defects and learning disability define it. Hearing loss 80-99%; clefts 30-79% omitted at cap; renal involvement frequency unclear.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none under the four-axis cap: defining orofacial clefts occur in 30-79%; retain more frequent hearing impairment and skeletal/ocular defects plus disabling intellectual impairment.
decisions.neurologic: primary: learning disability is explicitly defining, supported by the intellectual-disability parent and HPO frequency of 30-79%.

basis: The sequence is defined by urethral obstruction, renal dysplasia or hydronephrosis, and oligohydramnios-associated pulmonary hypoplasia.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary hypoplasia is a defining component of this named developmental sequence, rather than an incidental complication.

basis: Deep infiltrating adipose tumor typically involving skeletal muscle; subcutaneous involvement is not established across most cases. Tumor vascularity alone adds no vascular axis.

decisions.dermatologic: none: this infiltrating subtype characteristically occupies deep soft tissue and muscle; subcutaneous origin or involvement is not established in most cases.

basis: Inherited red-cell aplasia; congenital thenar muscle hypoplasia, recorded as small thenar eminence, occurs in 7/10. Cardiac and renal malformations are uncommon.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: small thenar eminence in 7/10 supports common congenital thenar muscle hypoplasia, a persistent structural musculoskeletal defect.

basis: Most cases across this umbrella are benign dermal or subcutaneous fibrous histiocytomas; deep soft-tissue and bone variants do not represent most patients.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: benign cutaneous fibrous histiocytomas account for most patients across this umbrella, supporting skin/subcutis as the predominant origin.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: deep soft-tissue and bone tumors occur in particular subtypes; mesenchymal histology alone does not establish locomotor tissue involvement in most patients.

basis: Segmental maldevelopment of the spinal cord and vertebral column defines the disorder; direct urinary tract damage in at least 30% is not established.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder can accompany cord dysfunction, but direct urinary tract injury in at least ~30% is not established; secondary urologic diagnoses do not suffice.

basis: Idiopathic chronic vulvar pain affects a reproductive site outside the axes; the definition establishes no nerve lesion or other covered organ disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: the neurological pain parent does not establish brain, spinal cord or peripheral nerve pathology; unexplained localized pain alone is insufficient.
